title: Chamier: faith is love (credere in Deum = loving) hence will-act
source_text: XIII. Hanc sententiam tenet Daniel Chamierus, qui probat primo fidem esse in intellectu, deinde etiam illam esse in voluntate. Et inter alia hoc argumento utitur; Omnis amor est actus voluntatis: At fides est amor: Ergo est actus voluntatis. Fidem autem esse amorem, inde probat quod vera fides est ea qua credimus in Deum. Credere autem in Deum, teste Augustino, est credendo amare. Panstrat. tom. 3. lib. 12. cap. 3. & 4.
pass_a_gloss: Daniel Chamier holds this opinion, who first proves faith is in the intellect, then also that it is in the will. And among other things he uses this argument: Every love is an act of the will; but faith is love; therefore it is an act of the will. And that faith is love he proves because true faith is that by which we believe in God. But to believe in God, Augustine testifies, is to love by believing (Panstrat. 3.12.3-4).
pass_b_english: Chamier: faith is in intellect and will; syllogism — love is will-act; faith is love; therefore will-act.
True faith = believing in God = loving by believing (Augustine).

choices.why: Fiducial living faith, not bare assent.
